about.title: Menlo Park Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Menlo Park's mix of office parks, retail corridors, and industrial stretches near Willow Road and US-101 means workplace injuries can happen in a lot of different settings, from delivery drivers navigating traffic on Marsh Road to warehouse staff handling equipment. In California, workers' compensation is generally the exclusive path for claims against your own employer, no matter who was at fault. But when someone outside your employer contributed to the injury, a subcontractor, a property owner, or an equipment manufacturer, you may also have grounds for a separate third-party claim. Untangling which path applies, and whether both apply, isn't always simple, and San Mateo County's employers and insurers know the rules better than most workers do. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we're a free service that connects injured workers in Menlo Park with an independent attorney who can look at the facts of your specific situation and explain your options without any obligation.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Claim

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Story
items.desc: California generally treats workers' comp as the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker may still owe you a separate claim.

items.title: Deadlines Move Fast
items.desc: You typically have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and any third-party claim usually carries a 2-year deadline, so waiting can cost you options.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal
items.desc: California law protects you from being fired or punished for reporting a workplace injury, and an attorney can help you understand those protections if you're worried about speaking up.

items.question: I was hurt on a job site near Willow Road, do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' comp is your primary route against your employer regardless of fault. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, or another company contributed to the accident, you may also have a separate third-party claim worth exploring. An independent attorney can review the specifics and explain which paths apply to your situation.

items.question: What if my employer in Menlo Park says I waited too long to report?
items.answer: California generally requires you to report a workplace injury within 30 days, so timing matters. If you're close to or past that window, it's still worth talking to an attorney, since circumstances vary and there may be exceptions or additional claims available. Don't assume you're out of options without checking first.

items.question: Can I be fired for reporting an injury at work?
items.answer: No, retaliation for reporting a workplace injury is illegal under California law. If you believe you're facing punishment or pressure for speaking up, an independent attorney connected through LawProactive can help you understand your rights and next steps at no cost to you.
